name: High Pulley Straight-Arm Pull (Facing Away)
description: The facing-away high pulley straight-arm pull has the lifter facing away from the cable stack, gripping a high attachment and pulling it forward and downward with straight arms. Unlike the standard straight-arm pulldown (facing the cable), this variation loads the lats through a forward-to-down arc that challenges them in both the overhead stretched position and the contracted position differently, with greater emphasis on the lower lat fibers.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing away from a high cable pulley. Reach back overhead and grasp a rope or straight bar. Begin with arms extended overhead toward the pulley.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the pulley to the highest position. Stand close enough that the arms are reaching overhead at approximately the cable's exit angle.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended overhead gripping the attachment.
Step 2: With straight arms, pull the attachment forward and downward in an arc.
Step 3: Continue until the arms are at approximately hip or thigh level.
Step 4: Hold 1 second at peak contraction.
Step 5: Return under control — arms travel back and overhead.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale on the return overhead.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — arms must stay straight
Leaning forward excessively to extend range — keep the torso relatively upright
safety_considerations: The overhead starting position requires shoulder mobility — assess before loading
Moderate loads only — straight-arm exercises have high moment arm demands
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arms overhead to arms at hips, maintaining straight elbows throughout.
coaching_cues: Arms stay locked — think 'pull the earth down'
Feel the lat at the top stretch
